title: General Manager Projects
minimumQualification: - B.E. / B.Tech in Electronics and Communication Engineering (ECE) or Electrical and Electronics Engineering (EEE).
jobDescription:
Qualification:
- B.E. / B.Tech in Electronics and Communication Engineering (ECE) or Electrical and Electronics Engineering (EEE). Preferred: M.Tech in Avionics, Radar, Microwave, Digital Signal Processing, or an MBA in Project Management / Operations. Ex-Defence Officers: Commissioned Technical Officers retired/transitioning from the Indian Navy (Electrical Branch) or Indian Air Force (Technical Branch) are highly preferred. Experience: 25 to 30 Years Domain Focus: Radars, Electronic Warfare (EW), and Strategic Communication Systems Reporting To: Chief Operating Officer (COO) / Head of Projects Role Objective The General Manager
- Projects will spearhead the execution, integration, and lifecycle delivery of complex defense electronics projects. This senior leadership role demands a seamless blend of deep technical understanding in high-frequency hardware and a disciplined, strategic approach to defense project management. The ideal candidate will bridge the gap between engineering design teams, production, and Indian Defence customers to ensure delivery on time, within budget, and to exacting military standards. Key Responsibilities
1. End-to-End Project Execution & Delivery Oversee multi-disciplinary project teams across diverse engineering verticals (Hardware Design, RF & Microwave, FPGA, Software, and Production). Establish rigorous project schedules, baseline execution milestones, and implement continuous risk-mitigation strategies. Ensure all systems are designed and qualified strictly to defense standards, including MIL-STD-810 (environmental) and MIL-STD-461 (EMI/EMC).
2. Customer & Stakeholder Management Act as the primary technical and managerial liaison for key defense stakeholders, including DRDO labs, Indian Navy, Indian Air Force, and defense PSUs. Guide teams through critical defense milestone reviews, including System Requirement Specifications (Sy RS), Preliminary Design Reviews (PDR), and Critical Design Reviews (CDR). Manage acceptance testing protocols, overseeing Factory Acceptance Trials (FAT) and Joint Field Evaluation / Site Acceptance Trials (SAT).
3. Cross-Functional Operations Coordination Collaborate tightly with the Supply Chain Management (SCM) team to guarantee timely procurement of highly specialized, high-reliability electronic and mechanical components. Partner with the Production and Quality Assurance (QA/QC) teams to streamline manufacturing workflows, environmental stress screening (ESS), and ensure compliance with AS9100 Rev D standards. Dynamically allocate resources across multiple active project streams to eliminate delivery bottlenecks. Solid experience handling the induction, maintenance, system upgrade, or trials of modern Radar systems, Electronic Warfare suites (Jammers/Receivers), or advanced tactical Communication Networks. Age Criteria Preferable: Less than 52 years old as of the date of application. Domain-Specific Expertise Radars: Deep understanding of radar signal processing, transmitter/receiver sub-systems, or active electronically scanned arrays (AESA). Electronic Warfare (EW): Hands-on exposure to SIGINT/ELINT systems, RF/Microwave architectures, or jammer power amplifiers. Communication Systems: Familiarity with high-speed digital designs, V/UHF software-defined radios (SDRs), and secure communication protocols.

title: Engineer - Radar Signal Processing
minimumQualification: BE/B.Tech or ME/M.Tech in ECE / EEE / Signal Processing / Communication Systems with 3 - 8 years of Experience in Signal Processing
jobDescription:
Qualification: BE/B.Tech or ME/M.Tech in ECE / EEE / Signal Processing / Communication Systems with 3
- 8 years of Experience in Signal Processing Role Objective As a Radar Signal Processing Engineer, you will be responsible for the design, simulation, and implementation of high-performance algorithms that enable radar systems to detect, track, and classify targets in complex, high-clutter environments. You will work on the full signal chain, from raw ADC data to target reporting. Key Responsibilities Algorithm Development: Design and implement real-time radar algorithms including Pulse Compression, Moving Target Indicator (MTI), Pulse Doppler Processing, and CFAR (Constant False Alarm Rate) detection. Modeling & Simulation: Develop high-fidelity radar system models in MATLAB/Simulink or Python to evaluate performance metrics like Pdâ€‹ (Probability of Detection) and Pfaâ€‹ (Probability of False Alarm). Implementation: Port validated algorithms onto hardware platforms using FPGAs (Xilinx/Altera) or high-performance DSPs. Collaborate with firmware teams for VHDL/Verilog implementation. Clutter & Interference Management: Develop advanced techniques for clutter suppression, jammer cancellation (ECCM), and sidelobe reduction. System Integration: Support the integration of signal processing software with RF front-ends and backend data processors. Field Testing & Analysis: Analyze real-world flight/field data to refine algorithms and perform Root Cause Analysis (RCA) on detection discrepancies. Technical Skills & Competencies Category Requirement Radar Fundamentals: Deep understanding of Pulsed Doppler, FMCW, Phased Array, and SAR architectures. Digital Signal Processing: Expertise in FFTs, Digital Filtering (FIR/IIR), Adaptive Filtering, and Multirate DSP. Tools: Proficiency in MATLAB (Signal Processing & Radar Toolboxes) and C/C++. Hardware Awareness: Familiarity with ADC/DAC interfaces, high-speed Ser Des, and FPGA-based DSP slices. Advanced Topics: Experience with Micro-Doppler analysis, Angle of Arrival (Ao A) estimation, or Beamforming is a plus.
